document.abstract: After the transition to file-based workflows, broadcasters and production companies are facing new technological challenges. New business opportunities encourage programmakers to tell their stories on multiple distribution platforms, but they typically lack tools and platforms to do so efficiently. Furthermore, production platforms should embrace the flexibility offered by consumerization and cloud paradigms. VRT-medialab proposes a cloud-hosted autonomous media production (CHAMP) platform that brings innovative production workflows to the cloud. CHAMP is a technology platform on which software and media infrastructure can be offered as a service. For programmakers the platform provides fit-for-purpose cloud web apps to collaborate on a multiplatform story, using consumer devices such as tablets. In this paper a set of innovative platform web apps are discussed that support a real-life documentary use case. To provide interoperability a flexible story-centric data model is defined. Also public and private cloud concepts are applied to enable high-resolution workflows.

authors.bio: Peter Defreyne is currently a media infrastructure expert at CandIT-media. He graduated as an electrotechnical engineer from the Leuven University, Belgium, where he specialized in multimedia processing. Defreyne started his career at VRT-medialab, the research department of the Flemish public broadcaster as a research engineer. He joined the group that optimizes the performance of IT solutions in media environments. His first expertise is focused on SAN networks, IP networks and workflow optimization on large-scale storage clusters. Defreyne's work on editing on generic storage was published at IBC and the SMPTE Technical Conferences in 2010. Since then he has been working on his first large project on innovative production workflows in the cloud. Defreyne can be contacted at peter.defreyne@candit-media.com.
authors.name: Peter Defreyne

authors.bio: Luk Overmeire obtained a MSc in electronics engineering from the University of Ghent, Belgium. Before joining VRT, he was a research engineer in Alcatel Bell, working on software-based services and ADSL digital filter design, respectively. In 2002, he joined VRT's research and innovation department where he first performed research in the signal processing area such as metadata-based video encoding and rate control. He presently leads the competence group focusing on media production and audiovisual content processing. Overmeire is a member of several European Broadcasting Union (EBU) working groups, the Advanced Media Workflow Association (AMWA) and SMPTE. Since 1996, Overmeire has been involved in patent applications and authored several papers presented at international conferences. He can be contacted at luk.overmeire@vrtmedialab.be.
authors.name: Luk Overmeire

authors.bio: Matthias De Geyter obtained a MSc in electronics engineering from the University of Ghent in 2001, after which he joined the image processing research group (IPI) of this university. In 2004, he started working in the VRT's R&D department, where he performed research on media adaptation and media exchange formats such as MXF and AAF and their use in system integration. Other topics of interest include file-based quality control and production systems in the cloud. In 2012, he joined the newly founded Media Innovation Center. Since 2001, De Geyter (co-)authored several papers presented at international conferences. His e-mail address is matthias.degeyter@ibbt.be.
authors.name: Matthias De Geyter

authors.bio: Rik Van de Walle received masters and PhD degrees in engineering from Ghent University, Belgium in July 1994 and February 1998, respectively. His PhD focused on magnetic resonance imaging. After a post-doctoral fellowship at the University of Arizona, he returned to Ghent, became a full-time lecturer in 2001, and founded the Multimedia Lab at the Faculty of Engineering and Architecture. — Van de Walle is a senior full professor at Ghent, where he teaches several courses, dealing with the fundamentals of multimedia, and (advanced) multimedia applications. His research interests include multimedia content delivery, coding of multimedia data, metadata technology, content adaptation, interactive (mobile) multimedia applications, and e-health. Throughout his career, Van de Walle has closely collaborated with a large number of research groups and partners in engineering, biomedical technology, sciences, arts, (digital) rights management, media, and communication sciences. He has been a member/secretary/chairman of a large number of committees, not only within his own faculty but also outside of Ghent University. Van de Walle can be contacted at rik.vandewalle@ugent.be.
authors.name: Rik Van de Walle

authors.bio: Wim Van Lancker holds a masters degree in computer science. He worked as a researcher at the Multimedia Lab at Ghent University until the end of 2011, investigating format-independent media resource adaptation and delivery techniques. His current interests include scalable video coding technologies, media content adaptation and delivery, video quality, video streaming, media content presentation, Semantic web technologies and multichannel publishing. — Van Lancker's track record shows his broad experience in research projects: he participated in projects about video quality assessment, error concealment, content adaptation and delivery, multichannel publication, in cooperation with several companies such as Alcatel-Lucent, VRT-medialab, Televic, Belgacom. His work has been published in scientific journals such as Multimedia Tools and Applications.
authors.name: Wim Van Lancker
